title: Digital Problems
goal: Report a digital failure, separate observations from guesses, and ask support about the next step.

runs.text: Frozen
means not responding in the described situation.
Crash
means software stops working unexpectedly.
Laggy
describes delayed response.
Down
can describe an unavailable service.
Error message
is displayed information about a failure. These labels do not explain every cause.

runs.text: The booking page keeps closing when I select a date.

turns.en: The booking page keeps closing when I select a date.

blocks.caption: Give a useful report · User & Support

runs.text: Harbor Browser and the error are fictional. Include the task, visible behavior, timing, and what you already tried. “The page won't load” is an observation. “Their server is overloaded” is a possible cause, not a fact established by a busy ticket sale.

study.title: Ask before repeating or changing something

turns.speaker: Support

runs.text: Would you like to try another approved browser for this service?

turns.en: Would you like to try another approved browser for this service?

turns.speaker: User

runs.text: Before I do, will that affect the form I already filled in?

turns.en: Before I do, will that affect the form I already filled in?

turns.speaker: Support

runs.text: Let's check whether that information has been saved.

turns.en: Let's check whether that information has been saved.

turns.speaker: User

runs.text: Also, I clicked Pay once. Can you confirm whether a payment went through?

turns.en: Also, I clicked Pay once. Can you confirm whether a payment went through?

blocks.caption: Ask before repeating or changing something · Support & User

runs.text: Don't treat every failure as proof that an order was not submitted. “I don't want to submit it twice” states the concern. “Please check the existing order first” requests a sequence. This example does not claim that changing browsers fixes the issue or that a payment has occurred.

You may hear “Try restarting” or “Check the connection.” Ask “Do you mean the app, the device, or the router?” if the object is unclear. “I've already tried that” supplies useful history. Actual troubleshooting steps depend on the product and saved work; this lesson does not provide a universal reset procedure.

blocks.caption: Connection during a call · Participant & Speaker

runs.text: Cutting out / breaking up
describes interrupted sound. A text summary is one communication option, not a repair to the network itself.

blocks.caption: Account and security concerns · User & Support

runs.text: Multi-factor authentication / MFA

uses more than one factor to verify access. Exact setup and recovery steps depend on the service. Ask “Where are the official setup instructions?” and “What are my recovery options?” Do not assume a single menu sequence applies everywhere.

If financial details may have been exposed: “I may have entered my card information on a fake page. I need to discuss next steps with my card issuer.” Verify the contact channel. The FTC's guidance supports using known genuine contacts; neither a friend nor this model can promise the money will be recovered or the account is now secure.

Fictional case: laptop, Harbor Browser, booking page closes on date selection, error “Unable to complete request,” three occurrences in ten minutes, other pages load; Pay clicked once, payment status unknown.
Give a support report. Partner asks the questions in the first model. Include observed facts and uncertainty.
Partner suggests another browser. Ask about saved data and the existing payment before resubmitting.
In a call, partner misses part of your explanation. Offer a chat summary and confirm the key point.
Report an unfamiliar sign-in alert through a fictional support exchange. Ask for official recovery information; do not use real credentials.
Solo: read support prompts and respond, then hide the case and summarize the problem. Later change the error rather than assuming the same cause.
Possibilities:

“Other pages work, so I'm not sure what's wrong.” “Please check whether the payment was submitted.” “Where can I find your official recovery instructions?” Check that the failure, uncertainty, history, and requested next step are clear.

Source note: [FTC phishing guidance](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-recognize-avoid-phishing-scams) informs verified contact and compromised-information scenarios; troubleshooting models are invented questions, not repair instructions.
